messages: Practice on a separate task: ask an assistant for a half-page, two-bullet update for a museum director. Write the request with at least two concrete deliverable properties.
Review your request. Naming audience, length and structure helps the assistant understand the deliverable. You may revise your request or explain why you would leave it as it is.
Practice on a separate task: a museum table lists visits by month. Ask an assistant to make each figure traceable to a source table and named columns. Write the evidence requirement.
A source name alone does not establish that it supports a claim. Consider whether your request links each figure to specific columns and, when needed, a calculation. You may revise it.
Practice on a separate task: museum visits rose from 50 to 60, and a draft claims 30% growth. Select the specific claim you would check, then ask for a calculation or compute it.
The calculation is (60 - 50) / 50 * 100 = 20%. A targeted check identifies the growth claim and its base. Explain what you checked, or describe anything still confusing.
Practice on a separate task: a museum draft says 30% growth, but its source counts are 50 and 60. The disclosed calculation gives 20%. Write a concrete correction to the draft.
A useful correction identifies the incorrect 30% claim, replaces it with 20%, and explains the initial-count base. You may revise your correction, disagree, or say what remains unclear.
